title: Separate authority
lesson: An agent can investigate and propose a release while a separate authorized execution path deploys it; approving that release does not grant the agent deployment authority.
limitations: Illustrative architecture: trusted execution checks enforce permissions; prompts and approval text do not.
The deploy tool abstracts a separate deployment identity; r42 abbreviates a release record binding artifact and target.
Authentication, token lifecycle, replay/race handling, compromised credentials, and rollback are not depicted.
Audio was analyzed for levels and synchronization but was not physically heard.
Self-reviewed independent cut; no comparative ranking or default recommendation.

transcript.text: In this illustrative system, the incident agent has read-only authority. It requests service logs, the read succeeds, and the evidence returns to the agent.
The agent attempts to deploy. The deployment tool rejects its identity at the execution boundary, and production remains on release r41.
The agent instead proposes release r42 to a human reviewer. The reviewer checks and approves that specific release record through a trusted review path.
The approved r42 record reaches the deployment tool. A separately authorized execution path checks the release and deploys it; production changes to r42.

The agent tries a direct deployment again and is still denied. It can still read logs, and production stays on r42. Approval of a release did not expand the agent’s permissions. The stage fades to black.
